mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate and increase in labor force participation (measured by PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions characterized by high consumer confidence and strong housing starts, the S&P 500 tends to experience positive returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates, leading to a 20-day forward return increase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of late-cycle expansion periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in total employment (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to positive equity returns as the market anticipates a stabilization of economic growth over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC for the joint signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-shock recovery regime, characterized by a rebound in industrial production (INDPRO) above 100, the S&P 500 typically experiences positive returns as manufacturing activity recovers and corporate earnings improve, leading to a 5-day forward return increase.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO > 100 during the post-shock recovery regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
